data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Decentralized networks are more resilient because they prevent 'cascading synchronization'\u2014the phenomenon where a large service's internal redundancy mechanisms (like automated failover) actually accelerate failure by shifting load to healthy nodes until they also collapse.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The services are part of a tight dependency chain where the failure of one small service halts the entire pipeline.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The 'redundancy' in the large service is designed with sufficient headroom to absorb the failover load.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In a decentralized network, the lack of tight coupling means that a failure in one service does not automatically trigger a load-shift to another service that may be susceptible to the same correlated trigger, thereby containing the blast radius.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
